items.title: Ukrainian war orphans' long road to healing: 'We don't talk to him about his parents' death. We wait for him to ask questions'
items.description: Thousands of Ukrainian children, whose parents were killed in the war, have been cared for in public orphanages with a post-Soviet structure, by foster families, or by non-profit organizations that have tried to heal their psychological wounds.

items.title: Yemen: 30 dead in strikes on Taiz market

Government forces and local authorities have disputed the claim, instead accusing the Houthis of indiscriminate fire. The province has witnessed intense clashes in recent weeks …

items.title: Ukraine Hopes Oleshky Can Serve As Model For Wider Truce, Delegation Says In DC
items.description: Ukraine hopes a temporary cease-fire that enabled humanitarian aid deliveries and civilian evacuations from the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky could serve as a model for wider de-escalation efforts, Ukrainian officials said on November 6.

items.title: In southern Lebanon, caught between war and peace
items.description: Despite a ceasefire deal reached earlier this year, the Israeli military still occupies a large swath of southern Lebanon.

items.title: Czech arms makers set sights on space defense in bid to sustain Ukraine-driven arms boom
items.description: Czech arms makers have thrived on demand linked to the war in Ukraine. To sustain their growth, they need to look beyond ammunition and toward new technologies — and even space.

items.title: World News in Brief: Civilians killed in DR Congo, Ukrainians wrestle with return, Guterres calls out ‘normalisation’ of force

items.description: The U.S. president did not disclose what he discussed with envoy Kirill Dmitriev, but he predicted a deal to end the war in Ukraine could emerge soon.
